stories.headline: WTA Chennai Open: New year, same damp squib as Cyclone Murasu washes out day 1
stories.title: WTA Chennai Open: New year, same damp squib as Cyclone Murasu washes out day 1
stories.summary: The weather in Chennai and the city’s susceptibility to cyclonic activity at this time of year vindicates WTA’s decision to relocate India’s only Tour-level event to the Philippines in 2027.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Rains brought in by cyclone Murasu led to a complete washout on the opening day of the WTA 250 Chennai Open at the SDAT Stadium in Nungambakkam.

The intermittent drizzle, along with a brief downpour, forced the tournament organisers to eventually call the day off around 6:40 p.m. soon after they had issued a revised order of play which featured just five singles matches.
“Between 8:30 a.m. and 5:30 p.m. on Monday, the Nungambakkam area received 8.8mm of rainfall,” an India Meteorological Department (IMD) official told Sportstar.
Therefore, the action on Tuesday, featuring all 16 first-round matches, has been brought forward by four hours and will begin at 11 a.m. to get the tournament back on schedule.
However, according to IMD, thunderstorms and lightning are expected on Day 2 as well.
The first edition of the tournament was held in 2022 in September, the week following the U.S. Open, amidst clear skies.
But when it returned to India in November last year, the first two days of the main draw were completely washed out due to rain.
The same is likely to happen this time as well, vindicating WTA’s decision to relocate India’s only Tour-level event to the Philippines in 2027.
Of course, the growing popularity of Filipino star Alexandra Eala is the bigger factor behind the move.
As per Tuesday’s schedule, all three Indian wild cards - Vaishnavi Adkar, Maaya Rajeshwaran Revathi and Sahaja Yamalapalli - will play one after the other on the Centre Court.

World No. 334 Vaishnavi, the top-ranked Indian, will be up against Jodie Burrage, the 27-year-old Brit who has entered the main draw via a Protected Ranking of 149 but has been ranked as high as 85th in the world.

After the 21-year-old Vaishnavi, Maaya will step on the court where the 17-year-old girl from Coimbatore, who recently clinched her maiden title at the senior level, will face Polish World No. 106 Katarzyna Kawa.

stories.headline: Cyclone Murasu Disrupts Air Travel in Andhra, 19 Flights Cancelled
stories.title: Cyclone Murasu Disrupts Air Travel in Andhra, 19 Flights Cancelled
stories.summary: Severe cyclonic storm Murasu is set to cross Andhra Pradesh coast between Nellore and Narasapur in the intervening night of November 2-3, the Meteorological Department said on Monday.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Cyclone Murasu is approaching Andhra Pradesh with winds of up to 110 kmph.
Authorities have stepped up evacuations and emergency preparations, while flights have been cancelled and schools shut in parts of Tamil Nadu.
Amaravati: Cyclone Murasu intensified into a severe cyclonic storm over the west-central and adjoining southwest Bay of Bengal on Monday, November 2, as it moved towards the Andhra Pradesh coast.

The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast that the system will cross the south Andhra Pradesh coast between Nellore and Narsapur, close to Ongole, around 11.30 pm on Monday and the early hours of Tuesday, November 3.
According to the IMD's latest bulletin cited in the updates, the cyclone is likely to make landfall with sustained wind speeds of 100–110 kmph and gusts reaching up to 120 kmph.
At 11.30 am on Monday, the storm was centred over the west-central Bay of Bengal, approximately 120 km east-southeast of Nellore and 140 km from Kavali.
It had moved west-northwestwards at around 14 kmph over the preceding six hours.
The weather department has also indicated the possibility of Murasu intensifying further into a very severe cyclonic storm before reaching the coast.
Heavy rainfall and strong winds are expected across parts of Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu and Odisha as the system advances.
The Andhra Pradesh government has intensified its preparations ahead of the cyclone's landfall.

Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu has directed officials to remain prepared, while Deputy Chief Minister Pawan Kalyan held a review meeting with officials from the panchayat raj, rural development and rural water supply departments.
Kalyan asked officials in Nellore, Prakasam, Markapuram, Bapatla and Krishna districts to remain vigilant and arrange the evacuation of people living in low-lying areas to safer locations.

stories.headline: Cyclone Murasu races across Bay of Bengal, IMD warns of storm surges up to 1.5 metres
stories.title: Cyclone Murasu races across Bay of Bengal, IMD warns of storm surges up to 1.5 metres
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Cyclone Murasu moved across the Bay of Bengal at speeds reaching 27km/h.
The severe cyclonic storm is expected to make landfall along the Andhra Pradesh coast early on November 3.
Storm surges of 1–1.5 metres could flood low-lying coastal areas.
Seawater could reach up to 330 metres inland in Ongole and 190 metres in Bapatla.

Severe cyclone Murasu is hurtling rapidly towards the Andhra Pradesh coast, with the India Meteorological Department (IMD) warning that storm surges of up to 1.5 metres could inundate low-lying coastal areas during landfall on the night of November 2-3.
The storm comes just days after the very severe cyclonic storm Arnab made landfall further north along the same coastline on October 28, 2026.

Murasu is expected to make landfall south of Ongole, between Nellore and Narsapur, between 11:30 pm on November 2 and 4 am on November 3, bringing strong winds, storm surges and possible coastal flooding.
What sets Cyclone Murasu apart is the speed at which it has travelled across the Bay of Bengal.
However, the storm slowed to 10 km/h during the six hours preceding 2:30 pm on November 2, according to the latest IMD update.
Rapidly moving cyclones generally have less time to intensify before reaching land.
The IMD forecasts that Murasu will make landfall as a severe cyclonic storm, with sustained wind speeds of 100–110 km/h and gusts reaching 120 km/h.
The cyclone is being continuously monitored by Doppler weather radars in Chennai, Machilipatnam and Visakhapatnam.

stories.headline: ‘Bada pataka’ under the counter, fake green labels on display: Banned firecrackers flood Delhi markets after Supreme Court nod
stories.title: ‘Bada pataka’ under the counter, fake green labels on display: Banned firecrackers flood Delhi markets after Supreme Court nod
stories.summary: The Hindu finds rockets, bombs and flowerpots sold discreetly in Sadar Bazar and Jama Masjid, with some green-labelled crackers lacking QR codes; vendors cite demand for louder fireworks as police seize over 1,100 kg
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: Hours after the Supreme Court permitted the bursting of certified green firecrackers in Delhi-NCR on November 7 and 8, traditional firecrackers were being openly sold, albeit discreetly, in Old Delhi’s Sadar Bazar and Jama Masjid markets.

A visit by The Hindu found vendors concealing banned crackers in cartons and black polythene bags beneath displays of green-labelled fireworks, with some selling conventional crackers without the QR codes required to verify their authenticity.
At least 10 vendors approached by The Hindu said traditional firecrackers, referred to in the market as “bada pataka”, were available.

One vendor opened his phone to show photographs of rockets, bombs, flowerpots and ground spinners, along with their prices, and said the items selected by a customer could be brought from a nearby warehouse in “five minutes”.

stories.headline: Jitendra Singh highlights expansion of disaster preparedness, weather monitoring infrastructure with new Seismological Observatory inaugurated in Kishtwar
stories.title: Jitendra Singh highlights expansion of disaster preparedness, weather monitoring infrastructure with new Seismological Observatory inaugurated in Kishtwar
stories.summary: Kishtwar, Nov 2: Inaugurating the new Seismological Observatory in the high seismic zone of Kishtwar today through the Ministry of Earth Sciences, Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science & Technology, Earth Sciences, Minister of State in the Prime Minister's Office, Department of Atomic Energy and Department of Space, Dr Jitendra Singh today highlighted the significant expansion of meteorological and weather monitoring infrastructure in Jammu & Kashmir after 2014, particularly in the erstwhile Doda district, with additional installations brought in after the Chasoti cloudburst tragedy last year. Addressing the gathering, Dr Jitendra Singh said that the India Meteorology Department (IMD) had strengthened the weather monitoring network in the region from not a single Doppler Weather Radar in 2014 to 4 installed in last 12 years and 4 more being installed making it total 8; Automatic Weather Stations from 3 to 12 out of which 4 for Kishtwar and 2 each for Doda and Ramban. Dr. Srinivasa Kumar Tummala, Secretary, Ministry of Earth Sciences, Govt of India, Senior Scientist Suresh and others came specially from Delhi for the event. MLA Padder-Nagseni Constituency and Leader of Opposition, J&K Legislative Assembly, Sunil Sharma; MLA of the Kishtwar Assembly Constituency and Shagun Parihar also spoke on the occasion. Deputy Commissioner Kishtwar, Pankaj Sharma and SSP Kishtwar Sunny Gupta were also present among others. The Minister said, the expansion of scientific and weather monitoring infrastructure has also strengthened the region's disaster preparedness in an area that is vulnerable to earthquakes, landslides and other weather-related challenges. The new observatory at Kishtwar is equipped with state-of-the-art digital seismic equipment and will transmit data in real time to the 24x7 Earthquake Monitoring Centre of the National Centre for Seismology in New Delhi. With the establishment of the new facility, Jammu and Kashmir now has four Seismological Observatories, including those at Jammu, Srinagar, Udhampur and Kishtwar. Dr Jitendra Singh said the observatory would continuously monitor earthquake activity in the region and contribute to a better understanding of its seismic hazards. The information generated would also support the district administration and rescue teams in responding more effectively, besides helping in planning safer infrastructure. Highlighting the transformation in meteorological infrastructure since 2014, Dr Jitendra Singh said that there was no Doppler Weather Radar coverage in the region earlier. After 2014, four Doppler Weather Radars have been installed at Banihal, Jot, Jammu and Srinagar, significantly expanding weather monitoring capabilities. He further informed that four more Doppler Weather Radars are set to be commissioned in 2027 at Doda, Kishtwar, Anantnag and Baramulla, further strengthening weather surveillance and extending coverage across the region. The Minister also highlighted the significant expansion of the Automatic Weather Station network. From three Automatic Weather Stations earlier at Udhampur, Kathua and Ramban, nine additional stations have been added, taking the total number to 12. These include four stations in Kishtwar, two each in Doda and Ramban, and one in Kathua. Dr Jitendra Singh said that the expansion of scientific infrastructure has been guided by the needs and geographical vulnerabilities of the region. He noted that administrative boundaries may change, but geographical challenges remain, making it essential to strengthen weather monitoring and early warning systems across vulnerable areas. The rainfall monitoring network has also been expanded, with the number of Rain Gauge Stations increasing from nine to 15 across the five districts of the parliamentary constituency. These stations provide regular rainfall information and strengthen local-level weather monitoring. Highlighting the reach of weather and agromet services, the Minister said that weather forecasts are now disseminated at the Panchayat level across all Panchayats in the five districts. The weather forecast and agromet advisory services have reached 5,467 beneficiaries, enabling wider access to weather-related information. He also referred to the strengthening of specialised meteorological facilities in the region, including the High-Altitude Cloud Physics Laboratory at Patnitop, Jammu and Kashmir. The meteorological infrastructure in Jammu has also been strengthened with the establishment of a Regional Meteorological Centre to provide weather and early warning services. Dr Jitendra Singh said that access to timely weather information has made a tangible difference to local administration and disaster preparedness. Referring to recent experiences, he noted that advance weather information helped the district administration plan and manage activities with greater ease. Emphasising the importance of public cooperation, the Minister said that scientific weather warnings can save lives only when they are taken seriously and acted upon. He recalled an instance when traffic restrictions were imposed following a weather alert and subsequent damage to the highway demonstrated the importance of adhering to timely warnings. “Information is important, but following the information is equally important,” he emphasised, calling upon citizens to cooperate with the administration during weather alerts and advisories. Dr Jitendra Singh also spoke about the need to counter unverified and alarmist information with scientific and evidence-based communication. He said that weather-related information and predictions should be understood on the basis of scientific assessment and credible sources. Highlighting the positive potential of technology and social media, the Minister said that access to digital information and new platforms has created opportunities for young people, including those living in remote areas. He urged the youth to make constructive use of the opportunities and facilities now available to them. Dr Jitendra Singh also reflected on the wider transformation of the region, referring to improved connectivity and the development of Kishtwar as a major power hub. He said the region's scientific and infrastructure capabilities were being strengthened alongside efforts to improve the safety and well-being of its people. The event was attended by senior officials, public representatives and other dignitaries.

From three Automatic Weather Stations earlier at Udhampur, Kathua and Ramban, nine additional stations have been added, taking the total number to 12.
These include four stations in Kishtwar, two each in Doda and Ramban, and one in Kathua.
Dr Jitendra Singh said that the expansion of scientific infrastructure has been guided by the needs and geographical vulnerabilities of the region.
He noted that administrative boundaries may change, but geographical challenges remain, making it essential to strengthen weather monitoring and early warning systems across vulnerable areas.
The rainfall monitoring network has also been expanded, with the number of Rain Gauge Stations increasing from nine to 15 across the five districts of the parliamentary constituency.
These stations provide regular rainfall information and strengthen local-level weather monitoring.
Highlighting the reach of weather and agromet services, the Minister said that weather forecasts are now disseminated at the Panchayat level across all Panchayats in the five districts.
The weather forecast and agromet advisory services have reached 5,467 beneficiaries, enabling wider access to weather-related information.
He also referred to the strengthening of specialised meteorological facilities in the region, including the High-Altitude Cloud Physics Laboratory at Patnitop, Jammu and Kashmir.
The meteorological infrastructure in Jammu has also been strengthened with the establishment of a Regional Meteorological Centre to provide weather and early warning services.
Dr Jitendra Singh said that access to timely weather information has made a tangible difference to local administration and disaster preparedness.
Referring to recent experiences, he noted that advance weather information helped the district administration plan and manage activities with greater ease.
Emphasising the importance of public cooperation, the Minister said that scientific weather warnings can save lives only when they are taken seriously and acted upon.
He recalled an instance when traffic restrictions were imposed following a weather alert and subsequent damage to the highway demonstrated the importance of adhering to timely warnings.
“Information is important, but following the information is equally important,” he emphasised, calling upon citizens to cooperate with the administration during weather alerts and advisories.
Dr Jitendra Singh also spoke about the need to counter unverified and alarmist information with scientific and evidence-based communication.
He said that weather-related information and predictions should be understood on the basis of scientific assessment and credible sources.

Highlighting the positive potential of technology and social media, the Minister said that access to digital information and new platforms has created opportunities for young people, including those living in remote areas.
He urged the youth to make constructive use of the opportunities and facilities now available to them.
Dr Jitendra Singh also reflected on the wider transformation of the region, referring to improved connectivity and the development of Kishtwar as a major power hub.
He said the region's scientific and infrastructure capabilities were being strengthened alongside efforts to improve the safety and well-being of its people.
The event was attended by senior officials, public representatives and other dignitaries.

sentences.text: Kishtwar, Nov 2: Inaugurating the new Seismological Observatory in the high seismic zone of Kishtwar today through the Ministry of Earth Sciences, Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science & Technology, Earth Sciences, Minister of State in the Prime Minister's Office, Department of Atomic Energy and Department of Space, Dr Jitendra Singh today highlighted the significant expansion of meteorological and weather monitoring infrastructure in Jammu & Kashmir after 2014, particularly in the erstwhile Doda district, with additional installations brought in after the Chasoti cloudburst tragedy last year.

The new observatory at Kishtwar is equipped with state-of-the-art digital seismic equipment and will transmit data in real time to the 24x7 Earthquake Monitoring Centre of the National Centre for Seismology in New Delhi.
These include four stations in Kishtwar, two each in Doda and Ramban, and one in Kathua.
After 2014, four Doppler Weather Radars have been installed at Banihal, Jot, Jammu and Srinagar, significantly expanding weather monitoring capabilities.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Censures TN IPS Officer A Arun Over Detention Order, Expunges Madras High Court's Adverse Remarks On Him
stories.title: Supreme Court Censures TN IPS Officer A Arun Over Detention Order, Expunges Madras High Court's Adverse Remarks On Him
stories.summary: An officer holding a senior position in the police administration is expected to appreciate the significance of the duties entrusted to him, the Court said.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: An officer holding a senior position in the police administration is expected to appreciate the significance of the duties entrusted to him, the Court said.

Observing that the powers of preventive detention must be exercised with great circumspection by the public authority, the Supreme Court on Monday (November 2) accepted the unconditional apology tendered by a senior IPS officer for an error committed by him while passing a detention order, and not apologizing before the High Court.

The matter arose from a detention order, passed by A. Arun under Section 3(1) of the Tamil Nadu Prevention of Dangerous Activities of Bootleggers, Cyber Law Offenders, Drug Offenders, Forest Offenders, Goondas, Immoral Traffic Offenders, Sand Offenders, Sexual Offenders, Slum-Grabbers and Video Pirates Act, 1982, classifying the first respondent's father as a “Goonda”.

The detention was based on allegations that the detenue and his wife, who were directors of a real estate company, had cheated a buyer after receiving over ₹1.38 crore towards the purchase of an apartment.

It was alleged that the apartment was not handed over despite execution of the agreements and payment, and that the property was subsequently dealt with in favour of third parties and mortgaged using allegedly forged documents.
A criminal case was registered under Sections 409, 420, 465, 468, 471 and 120-B of the Indian Penal Code.
The detenue and his wife were arrested on September 1, 2025.
The detenue's daughter challenged the detention order before the Madras High Court, which set it aside.
However, while doing so, the High Court made adverse observations against.
A. Arun in its judgment while quashing the detention order.
At the relevant time, the officer was Commissioner of Police, Greater Chennai.
The High Court observed that he was habitual in passing such detention orders.

stories.headline: NSA Ajit Doval holds talks with Vietnam’s Deputy PM General Phan Van Giang in Hanoi
stories.title: NSA Ajit Doval holds talks with Vietnam’s Deputy PM General Phan Van Giang in Hanoi
stories.summary: New Delhi, Nov 2: National Security Adviser Ajit Doval held talks with Vietnam’s Deputy Prime Minister and Defence Minister, General Phan Van Giang, in Hanoi, reviewing bilateral defence cooperation and agreeing to strengthen engagement in the sector. The Embassy of India in Vietnam said in a social media post that the two leaders discussed ongoing defence cooperation and ways to deepen ties. Doval arrived in Hanoi yesterday for an official visit during which he is scheduled to meet Vietnamese leaders to review the Enhanced Comprehensive Strategic Partnership between the two countries. The visit follows the elevation of bilateral ties during Vietnamese President To Lam’s visit to India in May 2026.

stories.headline: India moves to resolve Scotch tariff dispute, assures 75% duty on bulk imports
stories.title: India moves to resolve Scotch tariff dispute, assures 75% duty on bulk imports
stories.summary: The government is addressing a dispute regarding reduced import duties on bulk Scotch whisky imports. Liquor industry executives were assured that these imports qualify for the 75 percent duty reduction. The disagreement arose after tax officials questioned the eligibility of bulk shipments under the India-UK Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement. Major liquor companies, including Diageo and Pernod Ricard, have been affected by this dispute.
